note: v1 92.84 (seeds 0/11 92.84/92.85), Streetlight Hiss: trip-hop noir at 72 bpm, a rainy-night film score with a beat. A half-time break from the lofi-kit pitched down three semitones (snare lazy on 3, ghost notes, swung eighths) under minor mellotron strings whose harmony makes ONE LONG DESCENT across the song (Cm9 - Bb6 - Abmaj7 - G7b9, the last B lifting a minor third for its climax), while a gliding theremin-like boc-lead climbs against it (G Ab Bb B); a wordless vox pad in the B sections, a sliding sub, rhodes stabs in the second half, crackle throughout, and a bar of strings alone before each return. Drafts 80.9 -> 92.8: chords by section instead of every two bars (the bar-scale changes cut the song into twelve equal pieces), lighter swing, EQ to the lo-fi envelope.
